changelog: change: push_github.sh commits and pushes without asking. The y/N prompt was not adding a decision — nobody types this command by accident, and the answer was always yes — so it was a keystroke on every release and one more thing to be sitting there unanswered on a machine nobody is watching. What it printed is the part that mattered, and that stays: the file list, the diffstat, the count of new files and the full commit message all go to the terminal before anything is committed, so the record of what a push published is there whether or not anyone was looking. --ask (or -i / --confirm) brings the prompt back for a push you want to think about, --dry-run still shows everything and pushes nothing, and -y keeps working so nothing that already passes it breaks.
